desc:
You are given an array nums of non-negative integers. Perform these operations one after another for i = 0, 1, ..., n - 2 (using the values the array holds at that moment):

  • if nums[i] == nums[i + 1], set nums[i] to 2 * nums[i] and nums[i + 1] to 0;
  • otherwise do nothing.

After all operations, move every 0 to the end of the array, keeping the order of the non-zero values. Return the resulting array.

nums = [1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0]
after the operations: [1, 4, 0, 2, 0, 0]
result = [1, 4, 2, 0, 0, 0]
hints: Do what the statement says: one pass for the operations, then a second job for the zeros. Keep the two phases separate at first.
Operations only look at nums[i] and nums[i + 1] and only change them, so a simple left-to-right loop in place is correct (a zero created at i + 1 is then compared with nums[i + 2]).
To move zeros to the end keep a write pointer: for every non-zero value, put it at the write position and advance; finally fill the rest with zeros.
editorial: Phase 1 is a direct simulation: a single loop over adjacent pairs. A value is doubled at most once, because after a merge the right neighbour becomes zero and the left neighbour has already been compared with its right side. Values therefore stay at most 2,000.

Phase 2 is the standard compaction with two pointers: write is the next free slot for a non-zero value and read scans the array. Copy every non-zero value to write and advance it, then overwrite the tail with zeros.
Both phases are linear: O(n) time and O(1) extra space when done in place.
